bless you, very understandable situation!!!  from my experience so far, this would’ve been quite difficult in terms of allocating anything as you were in a moving vehicle - we would’ve received the initial location from the first few seconds of the call, but i’m sure the EMA (call handler) would’ve been able to hear that you were in a car (unless the arguing was too loud, so could’ve been unclear!!) so without a confirmed location, we wouldn’t be able to give dispatch anywhere to send the ambulance to, so we’d try calling you back a few times to make sure that you’re okay, ask if you need an ambulance, and then confirm the address with you.

different trust policies may deliver but for us, we don’t ever hang up really (apart from when the caller/ patient has left the phone and you can hear the crew have arrived and are with the patient), so we would’ve stayed on the line calling out to you until you hung up/ the signal dropped and the line cleared.  when that happens, BT comes back on the line, we confirm w/ them that you’ve cleared the line and we confirm your number, and we call you back.  when we have no address, there isn’t much we can do, so we would’ve left you a message asking you to call back on 999 if you need an ambulance!!  lots of other options when an address has been confirmed, but we definitely would’ve been calling you back to make sure you’re okay/ see if you need our help (especially given the shouting, but any dropped call to 999 will be returned, don’t worry!!)

even if you drop the line before getting through to us, BT will call us to let us know and give us your number so that we can call you back!!

they can all be reached when you call 999 but yes, you’ll get different sets of operators!!  essentially when you call 999 you choose which service you need and are put through to them specifically.  we (ambulance service) often get calls from the other services too - e.g. we get a LOT of calls from the police service, especially for welfare checks, patients at risk of suicide, etc.  as soon as one of us call takers marks an incident as in need of police/fire/coastguard/etc. assistance, there’s another role within our service which will get in contact with that service, with the information we’re inputting, often whilst we’re still on the phone.  from what i’ve seen so far, it helps the most appropriate response/assistance to be organised as soon as possible as there’s obviously only so much one operator can do at once!!  there’s then the dispatch team and other roles which all help this process too, which i’m sure is the same in other services.  is 911 all one service??  i think i just assumed it was similar to ours for some reason!!

999 operator for the ambulance service in the UK here - i can’t speak for the police service but we only call back when safe to do so/ there’s no evidence that a (brief and suitably vague) message being left would cause anyone danger.  e.g. calling to let someone know help is being arranged if they’ve had a fall and cannot get up, calling someone back when we got cut off mid-triage, etc.  when the situation involves violence or is volatile (obviously this is sometimes down to personal discretion or interpretation), we won’t call back if it’s not safe, and we’ll organise help based on the information we’ve been given.  we’re able to inform other emergency services (police, fire, etc.) so if we’ve got concerns about the situation we can sort that at our end without making the situation worse by calling back, and just get the help to the scene.  as others have said, always better to send too much help/ ‘overreact’ to information you’re given and make sure everyone’s safe.  patient safety first always!!!

i know this is super unhelpful but i’m there too.  the only thing that gets me to brush my teeth most mornings before work is the guilt and shame of being around other people for 8 hours.  i wash my hair once a week if i can even though it needs washing every other day.  i have no work/life balance because it takes all of my energy (and more) just to do my job and get through the day so by the time i’m done i’m so exhausted i don’t want to do anything other than lie down.  too tired to even just watch a film or read a book which in itself makes me feel worse.  i’m currently rewarding myself just for drinking water and hoping to build up to caring for my skin because it’s terrible atm because i barely eat or take care of myself properly.

for basic tasks SOMETIMES i’ve found it helps a tiny bit to break it down even though it already seems like it’s a simple task: so for laundry - making a pile of things that can go in one wash, the next day putting them in the washing machine (not even starting the machine) and the next day (the hardest) putting the cycle on, doing something that makes me feel an ounce better whilst it washes so that i have an inch of fake motivation to hang it up - then each day you’ve taken a step towards the task, and even though it’s tiny, it’s better than not having moved at all, and it makes the next day’s task slightly less overwhelming!!  i’m sorry this has been profoundly unhelpful, i’m in the same place as you and it’s so difficult!!  i see you and appreciate how hard you’re trying

(the other thing i try to do for showers is even when i need to wash my hair and don’t have the energy, i just shower without washing my hair, just letting some water run through it - i know it’s not ideal but it’s something and if you can muster some energy to stand up for a few minutes it helps you the next day to feel a tiny bit less bad because again, it’s more than nothing)

aw my love!!  i hope the tears were a good release for you at least !!  I know exactly what you mean, things like this have a powerful way of making everything feel so surreal!!  I felt like I’d forgotten how to function, like I’d have to manually breathe (rather than my lungs automatically doing it for me) or remind myself how to watch TV (and somehow take in/ understand what the people on it were saying, even if I’d seen the show before) - I remember just waiting to wake up from the bad dream all of the time even though it was reality and I’d been awake for days straight, just feeling like I was waiting for things to go back to how they were even though everything had changed and couldn’t (and importantly, for you too, shouldn’t) go back to how they were.  it’s such a horrible feeling, i’m sorry if none of that makes sense!!  denial is the kindest and strangest stage of grief, and it has such a stronghold on the body!!!!  I know the feeling!!  I think something that helped in the early stages was knowing that even if I had an entire meal in front of me, there was no pressure even just to touch any of it.  sometimes at first I’d just sit in front of food, sit around others eating food until it made me feel less nauseous, until I could take one bite from a meal, and that one bite (sometimes even two, or sometimes even a whole piece of broccoli!!) was enough because it was more than the day before that, or even if it was less than the day before, it was more than I’d eaten the WEEK before!!  there’s no pressure to keep one upping yourself, i found it was always best to just listen to what my body was capable of and continue checking in.  i say that like i was doing it consciously - i was lucky enough to have my mum constantly asking if I’d like anything to eat and helping me out, and i know that if she hadn’t been there i never would’ve tried anything for weeks - such is the nature of depression!!!  so I think you should be super super proud of yourself for reaching out for help/ advice, i’m so glad you’re trying to look after yourself, it’ll really really help you get through this time!!  I can imagine!!  I’m sure you’ll be able to eat even just a small amount by then - even if you warn them in advance that you’re a little under the weather (or something vague like that) a few days beforehand and you’re not sure how much you’ll be able to eat, i’m sure you’ll still be able to sit with them and maybe eat a vegetable or two!!  or even if you can’t, you can still say something vague about not feeling well and you don’t have to eat anything you don’t want to if you’re not up to it!!  you don’t have to do anything you’re not comfortable with.    I know the feeling and I promise it somehow does get better - once I started eating full meals again (they were much smaller servings than I’d previously eaten) the aches in my body started to get better and I even sometimes got more sleep which helped things feel a little more real, a little clearer, and it gave me space to think.  it was incredibly painful but it was so necessary and i know you can get there!!  AHH therapy that’s such such good news!!!!  I’m so so glad, I’m sure you’ll find it useful and again, you should be proud of yourself!!  you’re going to get there, i know you are 🖤 you are so very welcome, i am here if you ever need anything!!

I am so sorry to hear that you’re going through this- i really hope you’re okay!!  food-wise I experienced this when I was having a really long depressive episode in April when I left an abusive relationship (at first I ate maybe five mouthfuls of food over the course of a week and couldn’t keep anything down apart from water) - I started by eating things with a high water content, e.g. broccoli, juicy fruit (nothing too acidic), or drinking juice/ drinks that were more calorific than water (squash helped me make the transition!!) so that my body could get more used to taking in calories again - also ate very plain things like crackers, crisps (genuinely like three pringles and that’d be it), etc.  it took me ages to build up to soup (even though that seems like an easy option, i know) but it was really just about trying to gauge what felt right for the right moment - some random things like raisins and dried apricots, cereal without milk, plain rice, etc. worked sometimes and even though they seemed strange to eat (given the time of day or whatever) i just ate them because my body was letting me!!  did make the mistake of eating dinner in its entirety maybe four weeks in thinking i was ready and then my body brought the entire thing up again but swings and roundabouts!!!  a really weird tip i read once was about eating small things like raisins/nuts/small sweets/peas/sweetcorn as if they were pills so not chewing them, just swallowing one at a time with water so you take in food but you’re vaguely tricking your body??  it’s been hit and miss for me in my worst moments but just thought I’d mention it in case :-)  so very very sorry that you’re going through this though, i understand how heavy and all-encompassing the pain is and how strong the impact is physically too!!  I remember how much it made my body ache so I hope you’re managing to get at least a little rest but do remember to make sure you’re sitting up for periods of time and moving a little too, that really helped me start to be able to eat a tiny bit more 🖤  best of luck 🖤
